script:
This is the New Saint Croix Union. Wednesday's biography is Ted Kozlowski, Mayor of Stillwater.

Ted Kozlowski grew up in Stillwater from about the age of five. He has described the town as the place that gave him stability after earlier moves. He attended local schools, including Stillwater High School.

He studied political science and philosophy at Edgewood College in Madison, Wisconsin. After college, around the turn of the century, he went to the San Francisco Bay Area. He worked for nearly a decade in technology startups and venture work, from about age twenty-one to thirty. He has said one of the first companies he was involved with sold PowerBar to Nestlé for four hundred twenty million dollars. He has spoken of early work around Google when the company was small.

He lived for stretches in Madison, San Francisco, Buenos Aires, and Charlotte, North Carolina. He and his wife Rachael, a Woodbury native, moved back to Stillwater in two thousand six. They have two daughters, Amelia and Evelyn. Around two thousand ten they founded DemandQuest Marketing Institute in the Minneapolis area. He is its president and CEO. The firm trains businesses on digital marketing, Google tools, and related work. He has been certified in Google AdWords since two thousand five.

Before city office he served as vice chair of the board at Valley Outreach, a local nonprofit. He was elected to the Stillwater City Council in two thousand twelve, representing Ward Two. He has said the support of his hometown in that race was overwhelming.

In two thousand fourteen he ran for mayor against former council member John Rheinberger. Unofficial results showed him with four thousand six hundred forty-two votes, or about sixty-two percent, to Rheinberger’s two thousand seven hundred seventy. He took office in January two thousand fifteen as the city’s fiftieth mayor, succeeding Ken Harycki, who did not seek reelection. He has been reelected since, including an unopposed race in two thousand twenty-two in which he received nearly ninety-eight percent of the votes cast. His current term runs through January third, two thousand twenty-seven. He is on the ballot again in two thousand twenty-six.

He has represented the city on trade visits, including a mayoral delegate trip to Taiwan in two thousand nineteen and a trip to Japan with Governor Walz in two thousand twenty-three. On his own site he notes work on local events and trails, and that he is often on the St. Croix River or at Afton Alps.
